minutes_text:
VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 14, 2025
  2525 GRAND AVENUE, LONG BEACH, 90815
  , 5:00 PM

Kenneth Osborn, Chair  James Goodin, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Vice Chair  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner
Juanita Doplemore, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Osborn called meeting to order at 5:15 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade

Commissioners Absent: Schotter

Also present: Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Commissioner Doplemore led the Pledge of Allegiance.
  • Chair Report – Chair Osborn met with Councilmember Duggan’s office; the Councilmember
  and Chief of Staff are on board with the soon-to-be proposed recommendation to change the
  Veterans Commission to an at-large body and may provide assistance with a letter of support
  for the Veterans Administration, which faces harmful cuts from the current administration. The
  Chair also reported on the downsizing of the Pride Parade and festival this year due to the loss
  of major sponsors and a change in the placement of the VA contingency, which will bring up
  the rear this year, instead of its traditional placement at the front of the parade.
  • Staff Report – The summer meeting schedule was discussed. The next Commission meeting
  will take place on June 4, instead of June 11. No meeting on July 9. A new Commissioner (for
  CD 8) will be recognized at Council meeting on June 10. Commission vacancies and
  invitations to apply included in CD 9 newsletter. Candidates now under consideration for this
  district.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-55292  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of Wednesday, April 9, 2025.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner

  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

2.  25-55293  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Veterans Banner Program
  and In-Person Media Event.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Atkins Blade, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the
  following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

  • Staff liaison (Overholt) met with Long Beach Airport staff about the possibility
  of holding a Veterans Banner program presser. While such an event is a
  great option for promoting the program, with so few local reporters available,
  the Health Department’s Public Affairs Office (PAO) has recommended that
  a more grassroots social media-focused campaign serve as the primary
  vehicle for promoting the banners program. The PAO team will assist with
  producing content (reels and stills with captions) for this purpose. LBTV may
  also produce iClips (short-form videos) for its YouTube channel.
  • The Commission discussed the demise of local media outlets, and partnering
  with organizations that continue to produce their own media, such as
  CSULB’s media arts department (which produces a student newspaper).
  Creative coverage could focus on the tie-in between the USS Frank E.
  Evans Lost 74 and the Veterans banner program.
  • The Commission discussed other potential promotional opportunities through
  partnerships. Perhaps the VA Long Beach wants to do an event in
  conjunction with Veterans Day to promote the banners installed on
  Bellflower (next to the VA). The Commission could organize an informal
  event in collaboration with a local Veteran-led organization, such as a
  potluck in a local park, that brings together 2025 banner honorees and their
  families.

3.  25-55294  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the commemoration of the

  USS Frank E. Evans and Lost 74 to occur on June 3, 2025.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Doplemore, seconded by
  Commissioner Goodin, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

  • Staff liaison (Overholt) reported on a successful presentation to Council on
  the June 3 event the night before (May 13); survivor Steve Kraus and his
  family attended. Flyers will be available for distribution in the coming days.
  Discussion followed regarding flyer distribution with Commissioners agreeing
  to drop off flyers at the VA Long Beach (Ken), Century Villages at Cabrillo
  (Antawnette), American Gold Star Manor (Nick), and Council District 1 (Jim).
  • Staff will be distributing flyers through Parks, Recreation and Marine (25
  sites) and Libraries (12 sites) as well as sending out the social media toolkit
  to all Council Districts. the VA Long Beach and other local Veterans-related
  organizations so they can include in their e-newsletters or post on their
  socials. Commissioners are asked to attend the event and assist with the
  OVS booth.

4.  25-55295  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on a proposed housing project
  for Veterans at 1400 Cherry.

  A Laid Over was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Doplemore, Laid Over. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

  Commission discussion centered on providing a general letter of support for this
  item (to Council or Planning Commission) and showing in the meeting minutes that
  the Commission supports this item.

5.  25-55296  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on potential changes to Chapter
  2.60 of the Long Beach Municipal Code related to the Veterans Affairs
  Commission.

  Page 3 of 5
   VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 14, 2025
  2525 GRAND AVENUE, LONG BEACH, 90815
  , 5:00 PM

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goodin, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

  The Commission reviewed and discussed language for potential changes to
  Chapter 2.60 of the Long Beach Municipal Code. Approved language, “The
  Veterans Affairs Commission shall consist of nine at-large members, four of whom
  shall be veterans. No more than two Commissioners may reside in the same
  Council District. Members of the Commission shall demonstrate a concern for and
  dedication to the needs of veterans in the City.”

6.  25-55297  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on a recommendation to Council
  in support of keeping Long Beach Veterans Administration funding and jobs intact.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Goodin, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Schotter

  • The Commission brainstormed on the depth, breadth and quality of the
  services the VA Long Beach provides for local Veterans, including its PTSD
  Center, nationally-recognized spinal center, pharmacy, helping under housed
  and homeless Veterans become housed through its HUD-VASH program,
  services for transitioning service members and the disabled, mental health
  services in coordination with local Veteran serving-organizations. satellite
  clinics, administrative support with applying for (or appealing) service-
  connected disability and qualifying for PACT Act support, and more.
  • The threat of privatizing, curtailing or otherwise cutting back on critical
  services at the VA Long Beach jeopardize the health and welfare of tens of
  thousands of Veterans in Los Angeles and Orange counties. Ideally, a

  Council in August.

PUBLIC COMMENT

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Long Beach Pride Parade and Festival taking place this weekend, May 16 to 18. Future agenda
items: Commission Annual Report, potential partnership and event with Cambodian Veterans group,
changing the Commission charter in the future (per 9 members plus at-large members).

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Osborn adjourned meeting at 6:43 p.m.
